life_summary: David Allan Bednar was born on June 15, 1952, in Oakland, California. He grew up in California and received his undergraduate education before pursuing higher learning that prepared him for scholarly and ecclesiastical roles. Before his appointment to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, Bednar served as a university administrator and religious educator, earning recognition for his work in Church education. His academic background combined with his deep religious commitment positioned him as a thoughtful voice in the Church. In 1975, he married Susan Kae Robinson at the Salt Lake Temple, and the couple built their family while he advanced through various leadership and educational positions within the Church structure.
church_summary: Bednar served as president of Brigham Young University-Idaho before his 2004 appointment to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. He has emphasized spiritual development, revelation, meekness, perseverance, joy, and prayer as central to faithful discipleship. His teaching focuses on accessing living water through personal revelation and understanding things as they really are. He dedicated the Star Valley Wyoming Temple in 2016 and participated in the 2019 dedication of the Rome Italy Temple alongside his fellow apostles. His ministry has centered on helping members develop deeper spiritual understanding and a more intimate relationship with divine revelation.
